title: Ghost Key Eviction Interop: Runtime patch to stop pointer-alias KV leaks causing GPU OOMs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Several customers across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments reported intermittent GPU OOMs during steady-state traffic. Investigation traced the root cause to a pointer-aliasing defect in the key-cache eviction path: compacted tombstones and a delayed session handoff left 'ghost' key handles alive in the slab allocator. Over time these leaked handles prevented reclamation and triggered fragmentation cascades and eventual OOMs under heavy batching. Impact: multi-tenant hosted clusters (two SEVs), two dedicated customer incidents (latency spikes then OOM), and one on-prem private deployment reporting silent degradation. Scope: affects runtime versions <= runtime-1.18 when KV compact/evict race conditions meet long-lived sessions and bursty prefix reuse.
comments: 2026-02-18 Aisha Patel: Incident opened after two hosted customers hit contiguous GPU OOMs at 03:14 UTC. Triage: reproduce locally with long session prefix churn and accelerated compaction. Assigned to Marco for debug + fix.

2026-02-18 Marco Reyes: Reproduced leak in stress harness (kv_shrink test) — observed pointer alias where freed tombstone entries retained stale slab pointers when session handoff skipped index reconciliation under preemption. Filed a focused reproducer and memory map trace.

2026-02-19 Marco Reyes: Root cause analysis doc https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Ghost+Key+Eviction+Interop created. Identified 3 contributing factors: 1) non-atomic tombstone->compact transition, 2) session handoff path skipping index reconciliation under load, 3) delayed slab compaction heuristic tuned for throughput that defers reclamation.

2026-02-20 Marco Reyes: Implemented runtime patch: atomicize the tombstone->compact transition, add a lightweight reconciliation barrier in session handoff, and add a fast-path compaction trigger when free segments drop below 12%. Patch branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1427. Unit tests added for aliasing scenario.

2026-02-21 QA: Stress regression tests (48h) run in dedicated canary pool and private staging with workload replay of affected customers. No OOMs observed and memory trend flattened; CPU delta +2% on compaction bursts. Documented perf tradeoff.

2026-02-22 Ops: Rolled patch to hosted canary (10 nodes) with feature flag enabled. Observed immediate drop in long-tail memory spikes. Proceeded with progressive rollout to remaining hosted nodes and dedicated customer pools over 24 hours.

2026-02-24 Marco Reyes: Deployed patch to private customer staging and coordinated an offline upgrade window for on-prem deployment. Provided mitigation commands for ops teams (evict threshold override and emergency eviction script).

2026-02-25 Customer Success: Notified impacted customers with mitigation steps and timeline. For customers unable to upgrade immediately, recommended temporary configuration changes: reduce batch_size by 20% and lower KV retention windows to accelerate eviction.
2026-02-27 Security: Performed code scan and approved patch; no secrets or KMS interactions changed. Security review ticket: SEC-2026-37.

2026-03-01 Post-deploy: No new OOMs reported in the last 7 days across canaries and rolled pools. Closing as Done. Next steps: add telemetry for tombstone->compact events and an emergency alert when free segments < 15% for > 10m.

2026-03-01 Marco Reyes: Opened follow-up cleanup ticket to remove experimental compaction fast-path flag after 2 release cycles and to add a targeted microbenchmark for pointer alias cases (ENG-130101).
